title: The Drive: Get to Know Assistant Head Coach/Special Teams Coordinator Chris Horton | New York Giants
text: Coach Jordan, how you doing? Doing great, Shurmur. Good to see you, man. Yes, sir. Welcome to the New York Giants. Excited to be here. You look great in blue. I feel great in blue. I'm been wearing blue since college, so feel good. >> a little different shade. A little different shade. >> Yeah, but it looks good. Yes, sir. All right, so welcome to my Cadillac IQ, the all-new full-sized electric SUV. Very classy car. Yeah, here we go. Been a little whirlwind off-season for you? It has. It has quite different, you know, the [music] first first one in 12 years. Yeah, yeah, you've been you've been you've been there with with Harbs uh for 12 years, right? Down there just down 95? Just right down 95. Take us through how you went from being a player playing in the NFL to now all of a sudden getting into coaching. You know, it was one of those things where you know, once I was done, I kind of went back to UCLA and just really wanted to just wanted to see if coaching is what I wanted to do. Uh football has always been a part of my life since I was a young kid, so uh once I got that opportunity to coach at UCLA, fell in love with coaching, and then Baltimore started a program back in 2014. I was a part of that first that first intern program, and you know, I I didn't really know what to expect when I got there, but I always knew once I left UCLA, you know, what coaching was something that I truly really wanted to do. And to get the opportunity to go to Baltimore and coach start as an intern, uh really just paid off. And ever since then, it's just been working my way up. So, you fell in love with the game just from a different angle. Just from a different angle. So, you you start out as an intern, and now you're the assistant head coach {slash} special teams coordinator. What what what what is that responsibility? What does that mean? You know, I I don't take it very lightly. Um you know, I again, I spend I credit everything that uh John Harbaugh has done for me throughout my career. He really just put me in this in this position uh to be his right-hand man after after so many years. And you know, that comes with a a lot of responsibility. It comes with a lot of trust. It comes with a lot of understanding of, you know, uh getting the message across to to everyone and making sure that we're on the same page. As far as being a special teams coordinator, it was just something that was in me. It's always been in me. I started on the defensive side of the ball, but I've always wanted to be a special teams coach. Um I love developing players, and I feel like that's a that's a that's a room where uh at times it become a lost art. So, just to have the ability to just continue to develop guys and help them find their opportunity. You got a new [music] roster. You've got some new players. How do you go about assembling who's on those return teams? It's, you know, I think when you first get in there, you find out, okay, uh what can what can every guy do? You know, because [music] not every guy is going to be the same. Some guys and you just utilize their skill set. And I think that's what players want. Utilize me in a way that where I'm going to have success. And that's my job as the coach, figuring out what the player does best. Uh I might have a bigger guy, you know, that is a heavy-handed two-gap player, right? So, that guy is going to be utilized in a way where I'm I was going to be different than a speed guy when I start thinking about guys like Art Green, you know, so just just figuring out what every guy does. And so, the first thing I did when I came in, I need to learn the roster. Right. You know, so I'm sitting back, I'm watching the tape, I'm figuring out who's here, um what do guys do well, what don't they do so well, and then how can I help them do the things that they don't do well better? And then from there, we just start plugging guys [music] in places. And then as the as it goes on, we we build out everything from there. So, you're going to have a whole new battery this year, obviously. Snapper, holder, kicker. Um and that's obviously something new. Um how how do you go throughout that whole process? It just you start from ground zero, right? You you start at the bottom, and you build them up, and and you teach [music] them what you want. Um they're all good players when they when they walk in here, and you just make sure that you hold them to the standard. There's a lot of Some people will call it pressure. All right, I just say, man, you just go out there and you got to do your job. Cuz their their job requires a lot, you know, and when you're the kicker, there's punts always going to be involved. When you're the punter, you got to flip that field. And when you're the snapper, no one notices you until something goes wrong. Right? So, I just talk to them about holding each other accountable. And work from there. Yeah, amen. Well, listen, Chris, we appreciate the time. We are so excited to have you here as part of the New York Giants. We cannot wait for that opening kickoff. Yes, sir. Excited to be here. All right, thanks, man. Thank you. >> [music]

title: 1-on-1 with ESPN Analyst Dan Orlovsky on Free Agency & the 2026 NFL Draft | Washington Commanders
text: Commanders family. We have a very, very special guest here on Command Center for the first time on Command Center. Y'all seen him on ESPN. Y'all seen him everywhere football related. Dan Orlovski, welcome him into the building, sir. How you doing? >> I'm doing great. It's good to be with you, man. Good to talk some Commanders football with you. >> Oh man, I cannot wait to talk all about it. And I was like looking it up. I was like, let me look on Twitter and see Dan Rolovski/Commanders and see the kind of things he was saying. And you would do nothing but show love. So, we appreciate you, you know. So, I don't got to hit you with nothing crazy. I just want to talk about >> nothing too heavy. Nothing too heavy. Nothing too heavy. >> Nothing too heavy at all. But Dan, I mean, it shows that your poll, your finger is always on the polls. And it seems like the Commanders have been something worth talking about a lot, especially in NFL free agency. How do you feel the Commanders fared? How do you feel AP fared in this year's free agency? >> Yeah. Yeah. I'm bullish on on Washington right now. And it it's interesting because full transparency coming off of Jaden's rookie year and kind of that magical year of 24, I was a little bit more hesitant on 25 just because 24 was so magical and these comebacks and you had these fourth down conversions and it kind of at least I thought like overshadow a little bit of like where this rebuild was and you know some unfortunate stuff, injuries, all that stuff happens in 24 and then you go into, excuse me, into 25 and now you're into 26 in the start of the 26 offseason. It's Washington's quietly had this this unnoticed or untalked about but really strong season. You know, like you looked at this football team and you said, "Okay, first of all, you have this new offensive coordinator hire and David Blau that's probably a little bit of this unknown, but he comes from some really good football background both as a player and then coaches that he's been and system that he's been around in the NFL." And then you look at some of the defensive pieces, obviously a new defensive coordinator as well, but some of the defensive pieces you add, you had two edge rushers, edge rushers, Taan had such an outstanding year in New England. always still just scratching the surface if you talk to defensive people and the way that they can get after the passer. I've been a Leo Chanel guy since calling his games at Wisconsin. Just a just a big time football player at linebacker. Nick Cross from Indy's a really good addition. Just a smart smart safety. Um I'm a CHIG guy as well at tight end. I just think if you just put him with a good quarterback, you'll see the numbers and production go up. Um, and so like you're watching this organization just, you know, get younger, get more athletic, get more versatile pieces. And so, uh, I I think it's been a, for some reason, quiet, um, from the national perspective, but very strong offseason. >> I'm I'm very shocked to hear you say it is so quiet, I guess, for us because we're in house, right? It's been very very loud. There's been a lot of celebration on what Adam Peters was able to accomplish, but you said it's been a little quiet, maybe even a little underrated. Is it fair to say that maybe you think the Commanders may have won free agency when it's all said and done? >> Yeah, I think you when you look at teams, it's always like we we the free agency world in the NFL is almost extremes. It it's the who spent the most money and then we automatically and there's been some recent um evidence to say that that that is going to equate to wins. So you like who spent the most money? They've had the best offseason or they won free agency or you know this team that maybe they didn't spend anything because they're in that they don't have it. Um they're in a win now mode. They've already paid all those those players. And I I I think it's just you know the win free agency. Yes. Because there wasn't necessarily the massive contract that doled out that maybe everyone scratched their head at. And I don't want to minimize OA got paid a lot of money, but again, a lot of people sit there and say Ooway's just scratching the surface. I think he fits kind of the the the scheme that they're going to evolve to, at least expectationwise in Washington. So, um, yeah, I think that there was this almost like second iteration in this Jaden Daniels era in a way, you know, and it's so like yeah, the free agency you just check off is like a lot of really good pieces, a lot of really smart pieces added, a lot of winners too, a lot of guys that won like been was were around places that won football games and it seemed like there was an emphasis on that, right? like bringing guys and especially on the defensive side of the ball. You have a guy in Leo that you mentioned, two Super Bowls, three Super Bowl appearances. We have a bunch of different guys, Odaf who was able to break records in the playoffs as far as sacks are concerned. So, we got guys with that playoff potential. And I want to talk about this defense because we all know that the Commanders really struggled on defense last year, but now we have a new defensive coordinator and Donte Jones. Now, we add all of these different pieces. cuz I got to imagine you and the people that you talk to on a regular basis see the commanders defense taking a big move up this year. >> Oh, huge. Huge. And it's going to be for me. I think the most interesting part is like who are they going to be identitywise? Because I would tell you Dan Quinn's past, brilliant coach, but his past and Dante at least the experience that I would imagine he gathered in Minnesota, it's a little different. You know, Dan is a little bit more of like I'm going to line up and play one certain coverage and we're going to come after you and there's going to be this chess piece that we move around a little bit like Micah Parsons and I know it's his Seattle background maybe is a little bit more covered three and then Donte you know if you know anything about bean Flores the defense according to Minnesota it's I call it Star Wars you know it's this this all these moving pieces and all these different pressures and coverages and it's uh in a a little bit like maybe unstructured chaos. Um, but they get to their places and so it's going to be very interesting to watch the the the brain trust and the scheme and kind of what do they hang their hat on because I kind of live in a world if you look at the defenses right now in the NFL, it's you don't necessarily want to be predictable in what you do. You also don't want to be overly creative in what you do because then there's there's no cornerstone to your defense. So I think scheme wise. So I think it'll be interesting to see just defensively what do they settle on and who they are. And then I still think in this will lead to the draft is okay. Well, who's really like the the matchup piece for them? Got two good edge rushers now. But I still believe that those really good defensive coaches have just that piece. Dan Quinn being one of them. Just that piece that they can move around to create matchups almost like offenses do. But yeah, I I think that this defense is just from a youth athleticism and and um skill standpoint is much improved. >> So when you look at the number seven pick, because you mentioned the draft, do you feel that there's going to be somebody there at number seven that is that defensive course? I don't put you on a spot here, but I have to ask because it sounds as if maybe you're seeing them maybe maybe go that route. >> Yeah, I think the seven pick is is I think the whole NFC East is really interesting draftwise. Um, but I think it's interesting because I could sit here and unequivocally tell tell you like, yeah, if there's a player that a Caleb DS or a Sunny Styles falls, both Ohio State guys, you sit there and say you just it makes a lot of sense to have a piece like that. I'll go to Dante. A huge part of Minnesota's defensive success is having a safety. And I'll put up a Harrison Smith type of safety that was super smart, could be a great liar with coverages, understood everybody's job, and everyone says that about a Caleb DS or you say the Sunny Styles type of player that is that change, move, piece, crazy athlete. I can get him in rush situations. You get Okay. But then I could also go, well, I could see if a Jeremiah Love falls to them. I don't want to say false, but is available at seven. You know, then you go, man, could you replicate the Jaylen Herd Saquon Barkley running attack of 2024? or for Carnell Tate the wide receiver from Ohio State goes and says because David Blau I think of David Blau and I go okay David Blau was in Minnesota when they had a Justin Jefferson and two wide receivers said maybe it's an Addison or a Theelin and then he's in Detroit when they had Jameson Williams and I'm on Ross St. Brown. Okay. Well, we know they have Terry McLaren, you know. So, what happens if a Carnell Tate is there or Jordan Tyson's there? Like, do they want that second wide receiver piece? That's why I think there's a lot of available options. >> And I mean, that's a great position to be in, right? And I think that the way AP and DQ tackled free agency is why we can sit and speculate. I think a couple months ago, we were pretty locked in and saying, "Okay, we're probably going to get a defensive guy." But now, like you say, you mention a guy like Jeremiah Love. And I think when you hear a name like that and you hear a team in the commanders who were just two years ago in the NFC Championship just just this close, right? >> You get a guy like Jeremiah Love and you say, "Man, he might be able to get us to that promised land." I look at Jaden Daniels and Jeremiah Love in the RPO in the Renzo and you say, "How do you guard that?" When you look at a guy like Jeremiah Love, do you think he is one of those players that could take this offense to the next level? >> I think he takes any offense to the next level. I think he's 1500 yards when he steps onto the field as a rookie in the NFL. Uh just and I've this has been a parade of mine this off season. We we cannot just box him into running back. Yes, he's going to play that position, but he is so versatile and athletic in the things that you can do. There are people who are widely respected that would sit there and tell you if you had him just play wide receiver in the slot, he'd catch 60 plus patches passes just as a slot receiver in the NFL. And to context it, everyone knows that Jir Gibbs is one of the great backs in the in the NFL, one of the great football players in the NFL, let alone young. He's three in bigger than Jir Gibbs. He's 15 lbs heavier and he ran the same speed just for the context. You mean he had his average touchdown at Notre Dame was 36 yards average. So it you you're talking about just a a uniquely gifted player. And so um I think he changes any offenses and certainly and that's why I'll continue to point to like David Blau where was he last as a player? Detroit he was there when they took Jir. So, it's just like you've got a guy that has a little bit of just a vantage point of hearing coaches talk about this type of player and then watching how teams defensively handled this type of player. Yeah. And I I I just think um you know, if you attach him to an offense that has an improved offensive line, has this dynamic quarterback, has some good young pieces at tight end and wide receiver group that, you know, includes Terry McLaren. Yeah, I love it, >> man. Listen, if the fans weren't already begging their hands on the table, say, "Get us Jeremiah Love." When you broke that down, they might be sold. Now, my final question for you, Dan, cuz I know you're a very, very busy guy. We talked about Jaden and you mentioned his second year and all the things that went into that, right? Like, it was injuries, it was losing a loved one, it was going through personal things in life and also just going through being a sophomore in the NFL, which I know you know is very, very tough. But now you look at year three. And year three is that year for those quarterbacks where you really feel like you know what you're getting. What are you expecting to see from Jaden Daniels in 2026? >> Yeah, I would fully expect this massive step from at least last year and kind of the what we thought would be the runway from year one to year two. You know, that year one that was so magical. And you know, it's also you go through a training camp and your best receiver is not there. So, it's there's just so many butterflies, you know, attached to kind of not having Terry there last year. And so I think now with this new offense and and some of these new pieces, I there's no bigger fan of Jaden than mine than than me. I think people know that going back to some of my thoughts pre-draft process. And so healthy, no question. You want to keep him healthy. I love if the offense is going to be kind of what I expect it to be. And there's a there's a small part. I married a girl from Philadelphia. Okay. Dan, again, thank you so much for your time, man. And you enjoy yourself. We know it's about to get pretty busy. You enjoy the draft, bro. Hey, >> appreciate
